source.extractedQuestion: Represent each of the given relations by (a) an arrow diagram, (b) a graph and (c) a set in roster form, wherever possible.
source.extractedSubpart: (ii) {(x,y)|y = x+3, x, y are natural numbers < 10}
source.note: Direct extraction from 2025 English textbook; PDF page image not visually inspected.

stepsEnglish: For each x, calculate y by adding 3.
x = 1 gives y = 4; x = 2 gives y = 5; continue in the same way.
x = 6 gives y = 9, the largest allowed y. If x is 7, 8 or 9, y is 10, 11 or 12 and is not below 10.
Arrow diagram: connect 1 → 4, 2 → 5, 3 → 6, 4 → 7, 5 → 8 and 6 → 9; other x-values have no arrows.
Graph: plot exactly the six ordered pairs. They lie on y = x + 3, but the relation contains only these discrete points, so do not draw a continuous line.
